messages.content: Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does S16XAL do?
S16XAL is the Series 1600 symbolic cross assembler. It translates ASCII alphanumeric assembly source into binary object-module forms for 16-bit Series 1600 processors.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
Which literal formats does S16XAL support?
Octal, decimal, hexadecimal, and ASCII character literals.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How many passes does S16XAL use?
Two. Pass one builds the symbol table; pass two translates mnemonics, resolves references, reports errors, and emits object code and an optional listing.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What output follows an absolute assembly?
S16XAL produces an absolute load module. It can be loaded directly by S16SIM or prepared for loading by the resident loader.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
When does S16XAL produce a relocatable object module that needs linking?
When the source has global definitions, external definitions, or external references. S16LNK combines such modules into a relocatable load module.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What are the fields of an S16XAL source statement?
In order: optional label, required operator, operand when that operator needs one, and optional comment.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
Where must a label appear and how long can it be?
It must start in column one. It may contain at most six characters; longer labels are diagnosed and truncated after six characters.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What can start an S16XAL label?
A letter A–Z, dollar sign, question mark, or ampersand. The remaining characters cannot include a blank.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How is an unlabeled operator positioned?
If no label is present, at least one blank must precede the operator.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How are multiple operands separated?
With commas; the operand itself follows the operator after at least one blank.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How do comments work in S16XAL source?
A semicolon begins the optional comment field. A line whose first nonblank is a semicolon is a whole-line comment; comments appear in listings but do not affect assembly.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What special symbol represents the current assembly location counter?
An exclamation point, !.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What radix is the default for assembler numeric literals?
Octal is the default radix.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How is a hexadecimal literal written in S16XAL?
With X followed by a quoted hexadecimal digit string, such as X'1A2F'. An optional sign may precede it.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How are one- and two-character ASCII literals packed?
One character occupies the low byte with a zero high byte. With two characters, the first goes in the low byte and the second in the high byte.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What expression operators are allowed, and is precedence available?
Only + and - are allowed. Up to six elements are evaluated strictly left to right; parentheses are not supported.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does REL do, and what is the default assembly mode?
REL requests relocatable assembly and may assign a six-character module name. If neither REL nor ABS is specified, relocatable assembly is the default.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
When must REL or ABS occur?
Before any data-generating operator is processed. Otherwise the assembler reports an informative diagnostic and generates an unnamed relocatable object module.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does ABS do?
It requests an absolute assembly. Its output is an absolute load module that cannot be relocated or linked when loaded.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How do ENTR, GLOB, and EXT differ?
ENTR sets the program entry point. GLOB makes labels defined in this unit available to other units. EXT declares symbols supplied as globals by another unit.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What do ORG and EQU do?
ORG sets the assembly location counter to an expression. EQU assigns an operand value to its label; it can use a symbol, literal, or the current-location symbol !.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
Compare RES and ZERO.
Both allocate a block of the requested length. RES leaves the contents undefined; ZERO initializes the allocated words to zero.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What do BITS and MEML control?
BITS sets the memory-word width used for generated-data magnitude checks; its default is 16 bits. MEML sets lower and upper address limits used to validate generated-code addresses.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
Compare WORD, BYTE, and TEXT directives.
WORD emits one data word per expression. BYTE emits two 8-bit data bytes per expression for double-byte addressing. TEXT packs seven-bit ASCII characters two per word, low byte first.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What do END and EOT mean?
END ends the program assembly at the preceding statement. EOT marks the end of a source tape and separates source programs on that tape.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What are NLST and LST for?
NLST suppresses source statements in the listing; LST resumes their listing. Both are useful for controlling listing verbosity.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How do IFEQ, IFNE, and ENDC support conditional assembly?
IFEQ assembles following statements only when its expression is zero; IFNE does so when it is nonzero. ENDC terminates the conditional block.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does S16XAL ask for interactively?
It requests the source file and account, a listing choice (none, terminal, or named file), and then the object-file name. A blank source-file response returns to the operating system.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does S16LNK do?
It links two or more relocatable S16XAL object modules into one relocatable load module for S16SIM.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does S16LNK resolve?
It resolves global symbol declarations and satisfies external references while relocating and combining modules.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How does S16LNK's two-pass operation work?
The first pass constructs global-symbol data and a load-module memory map. The second rereads modules to create the load-module file.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What happens to an unsatisfied external during S16LNK linking?
The linker reports it, assigns the symbol value zero, and continues linking.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
Can S16LNK link an ABS module?
No. The manual says a module declared absolute is not relocatable and cannot be linked.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What is S16SIM for?
S16SIM is a debugging simulator. It executes Series 1600 instructions in a simulated processor environment so program flow and dynamic conditions can be inspected before hardware execution.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does S16SIM simulate beyond instructions and memory?
It supports simulated I/O data files, external interrupts and branch conditions, terminal I/O, traps/traces, varying memory configurations, timing, and stack-depth measurement.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What are S16SIM's initial CPU conditions?
R0–R7 and S/Z/C/OV start at zero; interrupts and double-byte data are disabled; privileged mode is active; CPU cycle time defaults to 400 ns.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What default memory configuration does S16SIM establish?
It initializes RAM at bus addresses 0 through 167767 octal to zero, uses 700 ns external-bus accesses, and maps terminal simulation at 167775–167777 octal.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How many memory parameter sets can S16SIM hold?
Up to eight sets of memory-definition parameters.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What is the simulator's execution-address history for?
It retains the last ten program execution addresses so the programmer can retrace recent program flow.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What is the difference between an S16SIM trap and trace?
A trace dynamically displays activity when its condition occurs. A trap suspends execution at that condition, acting as a breakpoint.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
Why is a trap on R7 useful?
R7 is the program counter, so an R7 trap provides a program breakpoint and an R7 trace provides a program-flow trace.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How many simulated I/O devices and interrupts can S16SIM handle?
Up to eight I/O devices and up to eight external interrupts.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How are S16SIM I/O events scheduled?
They are scheduled from accumulated simulated execution time, relative to time zero at the start of program execution.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How many external sensed conditions can S16SIM simulate?
Sixteen. An undefined external condition always evaluates false.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What bus addresses represent the simulated teletype?
167774–167777 octal. Keyboard and printer status are at 167774 and 167776; keyboard data and printer data are at 167775 and 167777.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What command-string structure does S16SIM require?
A command begins with a verb and uses the documented comma/semicolon separators. It is limited to 60 characters on one line; elements after the semicolon may be symbols, literals, or expressions.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does LOAD do in S16SIM?
LOAD requests an S16XAL-generated binary file and optionally an address. Without an address, the module loads at its assembly base; multiple binary files may be loaded.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How does RADX select display radix?
RADX uses 8 for octal, 10 for decimal, 0 for ASCII, and 16 for hexadecimal. With no specified radix, it selects octal.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does TLIM do?
It sets an execution-time limit in microseconds. Simulation suspends when that accumulated time is reached; omitting the time removes the limit.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How does SUM help debug stack use?
SUM defines lower and upper stack bounds. Execution suspends if R6 exceeds them; the related DMXS command displays the maximum stack-pointer value reached.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What is the difference between Execute, Step, and Continue?
Execute runs from a specified or current PC until a stop condition. Step executes one instruction. Continue resumes from the current location after stepping, a trap, or HLT.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What can stop Execute when no final address is supplied?
HLT, a user BREAK interrupt, an exceeded time limit, or a trap condition can stop it.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does EDR add to execution?
It executes like Execute but displays the registers after each instruction.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does DR display?
The contents of R0–R7, status bits S/Z/C/OV, INTPF, and NONINT.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What are DA, SA, and IA used for?
DA displays an address range. SA searches a range using a value and mask. IA initializes a range using a value and mask.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How does an MT entry distinguish traps from traces?
Its mode selects: 0 trap on reference, 1 trace on reference, 2 trap on content change, or 3 trace on content change. Optional frequency, value, and mask refine the trigger.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does an RT entry monitor?
A selected CPU register. Its modes mirror MT: trap or trace on reference or on a contents change, optionally gated by frequency, value, and mask.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How is an I/O buffer register defined?
IOBR assigns a table entry to a bus address and direction. Direction 0 is output and direction 1 is input; output is the default.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
How does an S16SIM interrupt-table entry determine priority?
INT uses an entry number 0–7, and higher entry numbers mean higher relative priority; 7 is highest.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does S16XRF produce?
A symbol cross-reference listing: each symbol, its definition line, and every reference line. This is useful when debugging or changing large assembly programs.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What are the stated S16XRF-1 limits?
Version 1 accommodates 300 symbols and 1200 symbol references, subject to host-memory capacity.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does S16BPT generate and why?
It punches an assembler object module or linker load module to paper tape so a host-built program can be loaded on a Series 1600 microprocessor system.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What does S16RTG generate?
It converts a S16XAL or S16LNK load module into ROM data patterns for General Instrument's ROM-manufacturing process.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
Why does S16RTG ask for a relocation address?
It can relocate a load module before generating ROM patterns, so the module need not have been assembled at its final ROM address.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
What ROM-base constraint does S16RTG specify?
The base address must be at least the relocation address and its three least-significant octal digits must be 000; a 512×10 ROM occupies xxx000 through xxx777.
Teach the historical Series 1600 S16XAL tool suite precisely and concisely. State manual facts without assuming modern compatibility.
Why does the manual recommend ZERO rather than RES for unused ROM space?
RES or ORG can create unspecified ROM locations and trigger a non-sequential-addressing warning. ZERO explicitly supplies zeros for unused locations.
